definitions.explanation: Lacking physical coordination or manual skill. Unable to perform tasks requiring fine motor skills well.
Unable to express oneself well or handle social situations smoothly. Often used about one's inability to show feelings or communicate effectively.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}は{不器用|ぶきよう}だから、{料理|りょうり}が{苦手|にがて}だ。
examples.english: I'm clumsy, so I'm not good at cooking.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{不器用|ぶきよう}で、うまく{気持|きも}ちを{伝|つた}えられない。
examples.english: He's awkward and can't express his feelings well.

examples.japanese: {不器用|ぶきよう}ながらも{一生懸命|いっしょうけんめい}やっている。
examples.english: I may be clumsy, but I'm doing my best.

notes:
TWO MAIN MEANINGS:

1) PHYSICAL: Not good with one's hands
・{手先|てさき}が{不器用|ぶきよう} (clumsy with one's hands)
・{不器用|ぶきよう}な{手|て}つき (clumsy movements)

2) EMOTIONAL/SOCIAL: Unable to express feelings or navigate relationships smoothly
・{生|い}き{方|かた}が{不器用|ぶきよう} (clumsy at life)
・{愛情表現|あいじょうひょうげん}が{不器用|ぶきよう} (bad at showing affection)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{不器用|ぶきよう}な{人|ひと} (a clumsy/awkward person)
・{不器用|ぶきよう}ながらも (though clumsy, nevertheless...)

NUANCE:
Often used with a sense of sympathy or endearment. A {不器用|ぶきよう} person who tries hard can be seen as admirable.

CONTRAST:
・{不器用|ぶきよう} ↔ {器用|きよう} (clumsy ↔ dexterous/skillful)
